newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Poor market forces Singapore IPO pricing down.
newsitem.headline: Poor market forces Singapore IPO pricing down.

text.p: Companies seeking to list on the Singapore stock market are trimming their initial public offering prices to ensure a good response amid poor market conditions, analysts said on Wednesday.

"If the market does not go up and the overall market P/E (price/earnings ratio) is only 16-17 times, it will force them to make their pricing more attractive, back to nine to 10 times," Najeeb Jarhom, research manager (private clients) at Fraser Securities, told Reuters.
Sixteen IPOs have been launched since 1997.

Henry Chia, acting head of investment banking with Keppel Bank, said companies seeking to list on the main board had priced their IPO shares at a prospective P/E low of 11.8 times to a high of 16 so far this year.
Keppel Bank, which launched book store operator Popular Holdings's IPO on Wednesday, has priced the shares at a low prospective P/E of 11.9 times, or S$0.36 (US$0.25) each.
The P/E ratio is calculated by dividing a company's share price by earnings per share. In general, the higher the ratio, the greater the market's expectations for the company's growth.
"When sentiment is bad, underwriters work to place out more shares to funds which take a longer-term view as you can't depend on market forces," an underwriter with a local bank said.
Market observers added there would be a few companies that would still succeed with higher pricing.
One was Raffles Medical Group whose shares jumped more than 40 percent over its offer price when it listed on April 11, despite a high historical P/E of 21 times.

"It is the only IPO in the medical sector," said the merchant banker. The one other healthcare company listed in Singapore is Parkway Holdings, currently trading at a P/E of more than 30 times, he added.
Analysts said healthcare and food companies would attract stronger responses as they were considered "defensive businesses with steady income streams".
